title: Legal and Compliance Officer
description:
**Role Summary**

Priquant Ventures Private Limited is hiring a Legal & Compliance Officer who will be designated as the Compliance Officer of the Investment Manager under Regulation 20(17) of the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations, 2012.

The role owns the fund's regulatory compliance end to end and acts as in-house counsel on fund documents, investor onboarding and portfolio transactions. It is a hands-on position in a lean team, with reporting to the Managing Partner.

Key responsibilities

The officer is accountable for the fund staying compliant with the SEBI Act, the AIF Regulations, the AIF Master Circular and every scheme's PPM, and for the legal soundness of what the fund signs.

SEBI and regulatory compliance

* Act as the designated Compliance Officer of the Investment Manager and monitor compliance with the SEBI Act, AIF Regulations, circulars and directions
* Own the compliance calendar for all schemes: quarterly activity reports to SEBI, unit value reporting to depositories, benchmarking agency data, and other periodic filings
* Prepare the annual Compliance Test Report for the Trustee and Sponsor under the AIF Master Circular
* Coordinate the annual PPM compliance audit, track findings to closure, and file PPM changes with SEBI and investors
* Report material breaches to SEBI, the Trustee and the Board within the prescribed timelines
* Track new SEBI circulars, assess their impact on each scheme, and update internal policies and procedures accordingly
* Monitor investment conditions and restrictions: concentration limits, Category II leverage restrictions, related-party and associate investments, and investor consents where required
* Handle SEBI inspections, queries and correspondence

Fund documentation and launches

* Draft, review and maintain PPMs, contribution agreements, the indenture of trust and investment management agreement
* Run the regulatory process for new scheme launches through merchant bankers and SEBI, including responding to observations
* Maintain unit class terms, side letters and investor-specific arrangements consistently with the PPM

Drafting of agreements and legal documents

* Draft and negotiate agreements across the fund and the Investment Manager: contribution agreements, side letters, investment management and trusteeship agreements, distribution and placement agreements, and venture partner and advisor agreements
* Prepare first drafts of transaction documents, including term sheets, share subscription, shareholders' and share purchase agreements, debenture trust deeds and security documents
* Draft vendor, service provider and outsourcing contracts (RTA, fund accountant, custodian, valuer, technology vendors), NDAs and engagement letters for counsel and auditors
* Draft board and Investment Committee resolutions, minutes, investor notices, consent requests and regulatory correspondence
* Maintain a library of standard templates and clause positions, and keep them current with regulatory changes

Investor onboarding, KYC and AML

* Run investor onboarding: KYC, CKYC uploads, FATCA/CRS declarations, accredited investor checks and minimum commitment validation
* Act as the point person for PMLA obligations, including risk-based due diligence, record-keeping and suspicious transaction reporting through the Principal Officer framework
* Oversee capital call, distribution and transfer documentation; review distributor empanelment and distribution agreements
* Handle investor grievances and SCORES / SEBI ODR complaints

Transaction and portfolio legal support

* Review term sheets, share subscription and shareholders' agreements, share purchase agreements and debt documentation for equity and structured credit deals
* Run legal due diligence with external counsel and track conditions precedent and post-closing obligations
* Review structured credit documentation: PTC and SDI transaction documents, trust deeds, servicing arrangements and security documents
* Monitor portfolio company covenants, information rights and reporting obligations owed to the fund

Governance, conflicts and controls

* Maintain the conflict of interest policy, the code of conduct and personal trading rules for the investment team
* Keep minutes and records for Investment Committee and Board meetings and maintain the statutory registers of the Investment Manager
* Track NISM certification requirements for the key investment team and other associated persons
* Oversee cyber security, data protection and outsourcing compliance, including vendor contracts
* Manage external counsel, auditors, the Trustee, the custodian, the RTA and the fund accountant on legal and compliance matters

Qualifications and experience

The NISM Series-III-C certification is non-negotiable: from 1 January 2027, only certified persons may be appointed as, or continue to act as, Compliance Officer of an AIF manager (SEBI circular, 30 Dec 2025).

**Required**

* Qualified Company Secretary (ACS/FCS) — mandatory; an LLB is an added advantage
* NISM Series-III-C: Securities Intermediaries Compliance (Fund) certification, or willingness to obtain it before joining
* Working knowledge of the SEBI AIF Regulations and Master Circular, PMLA and KYC rules, the Companies Act 2013, FEMA, and the Indian Trusts Act
* Hands-on drafting & review of investment documents, agreements etc.

**Preferred**

* Experience with growth equity or venture transactions: SHAs, SSAs and secondary share purchases
* Exposure to SEBI inspections, PPM audits or scheme launches through a merchant banker

Skills and attributes

We want someone who reads regulations closely and applies them strictly, while keeping the business moving.

* Independent judgement, with the confidence to say no and put it in writing
* Precise, plain-English drafting for regulators, investors and counterparties
* Organised enough to run a multi-scheme compliance calendar without slippage
* Comfortable owning work end to end in a small team, without a large support function
* Discretion with confidential investor and deal information
* Practical with tools: compliance trackers, document management and SEBI/depository portals

title: Associate Manager - Drone Ecosystem
description:
**About QCI**

The Quality Council of India (QCI) is the Scheme Owner of the Certification Scheme for Unmanned Aircraft Systems (CSUAS), which was notified in official gazette by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on 26 January 2022. The scheme has since been revised and its scope enhanced, evolving into a Type based certification framework that covers Visual Line of Sight (VLOS) and Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS) UAS operations, and it also promotes the indigenisation and development of the domestic drone industry, contributing to the vision of India becoming a global drone hub by 2030.

**Role Summary**

As part of the team, you contribute to the development and operation of a national certification framework for UAS. Our work spans into designing and developing certification schemes aligned with international best practice, formulating technical standards, and creating certification ecosystems in partnership with industry, regulators, ministries, academia and other stakeholders, scale them through conformity assessment bodies. Deep understanding of the Drone Rules, 2021 and CSUAS is essential.

The next phase of this work is about collaborating with the industry on the segments that still need enabling, namely autonomous drones, Drone-as-a-Service and UAS traffic management, along with the digital transformation that simplifies compliance and the aggregator led facilitation that scales the use-case adaptation to advance the growth of Industry These are areas where the standards, the quality assurance mechanisms and in some cases the market itself are still taking shape, and the people who join us now will help shape the Nation’s Drone Ecosystem.

**Role & Responsibility-**

QCI is seeking professionals to support the implementation of CSUAS. The role will contribute to the development and operation of the CSUAS workstreams below:

* **Scheme Design & Development**
  : Conceptualise UAS related quality interventions that help the industry and the regulator, and develop and revise the scheme criteria, technical standards and guidelines that give them effect with a in-depth understanding of the Drone Rules, 2021 and CSUAS.
* **Research, Analysis & Knowledge Products**
  : Conduct rapid primary and secondary research on UAS domain and policy, including comparative study of standards and international best practice to draft standards for UAS and its components.
* **Report Writing & Deck Preparation:**
  Draft and structure reports, concept notes, technical circulars and knowledge products, and create data driven presentations for relevant stakeholders.
* **Scheme Operations**
  : Lead the day to day operations of the scheme and its projects, scheme documentation, deliverables, work plans, trackers and minutes of meetings and report periodically on developments; collect, clean and analyse scheme data and maintain its records, website and dashboard; propose the features and changes required in the dashboard to support operations; monitor scheme-related activities; coordinate with vendors and internal and external stakeholders; and frequently update FAQs.
* **Stakeholder Engagement**
  : Identify key stakeholders, analyse their expectations, and develop and execute appropriate strategies to work with them; manage and regularly engage multiple stakeholders i.e., regulators, Certification Bodies, manufacturers, assessors, technical experts, laboratories and academia to ensure timely information exchange and seamless coordination.
* **Business Development & Marketing of the Scheme**
  : Ensure quantitative improvement in the number of Certification Bodies; identify potential clients and partners for adoption of the scheme; market the scheme to increase its uptake; and develop a comprehensive plan to improve scheme processes and revenue generation.

**Eligibility Criteria & Requirements-**

**Educational Qualification**
:

* A Bachelor’s degree in Engineering in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related discipline is required. A Bachelor’s degree in a related engineering discipline, coupled with strong relevant experience, may also be considered for the Associate Manager role.
* An additional qualification in management, public policy, or conformity assessment ecosystem, or quality and compliance, or training in ISO/IEC 17065, ISO/IEC 17067, or ISO/IEC 17024, or ISO/IEC 17020, or ISO 9001 will be considered a strong added advantage.

**Experience-**

* Minimum 3 years of professional work experience in areas including manufacturing, R&D, operations, consulting (private or government), or testing, auditing or a managerial role specifically in drone industry, or should have experience with stakeholder management, or operating a certification scheme, or national program.
* Knowledge of the Drone Rules, 2021 and CSUAS is essential, along with knowledge of the relevant rules and regulations with respect to drones operations in India and type certification.
* Excellent Microsoft Office skills, strong verbal communication, and sound organisational and planning skills, with a proven ability to multitask and meet tight deadlines, are required.
* Experience in marketing of products and creation of knowledge products is desired. Prior experience of working with government agencies, regulators or CABs in any capacity (operations or consulting) will be preferred.
* Working experience in any programming language, or with dashboards and AI tools, would be an added advantage. Exposure to UAS design, manufacturing, testing or flight operations, including VLOS/BVLOS flying experience, will be preferred though not mandatory.
* Fluency in English, both written and oral, is required. Fluency in Hindi, both written and oral, is desired.
* Location for the role is based out of New Delhi, on a full time engagement, with travel anywhere in India or abroad as and when required.

**Technical Capabilities-**

**Strong Research Skills:**
Ability to rapidly identify, read, and understand dense, technical documents (e.g., government reports and research papers) and extract the most relevant information.

**Structured Thinking & Writing:**
Ability to break down large, ambiguous topics into a structured research plan and produce clear, logical, professional, and well-written outputs.

**Data Analysis:**
Comfortable with data cleaning, essential MS Excel functions, and creating charts. Experience analysing survey data using Stata, R, or Python is an added advantage.

**Visualization & Presentation Skills:**
Strong data-visualization skills using MS Office Suite, with Tableau/Power BI proficiency being an added advantage; ability to create well-structured and visually compelling presentations.

**Behavioural Capabilities-**

**High Degree of Curiosity:**
Genuine interest in how India’s public policy and governance systems work; naturally follows current affairs and asks “why.”

**Integrity & Accountability:**
Takes ownership of tasks, delivers on commitments, and upholds the highest ethical standards in all work and workplace interactions.

**Meticulous Attention to Detail:**
Able to identify typos, formatting errors, inconsistencies, and mismatched numbers that others may overlook.

**Proactive & “Get-it-Done” Attitude:**
Self-starter who takes complete ownership of tasks, anticipates what needs to be done, and delivers results without waiting for instructions.

title: Legal Compliance Manager - APMEA
description:
**Position Title:**
Legal & Compliance Manager

**Scope:**
Primary responsibility for data protection and privacy in APMEA deployment of RBC compliance policies and programs in the region and the local implementation in India, and for provision of legal support to India GBS. The role may also support English-speaking countries in the APMEA region, as designated by the Regional General Counsel.

**Reports to:**
Regional General Counsel, APMEA

**Team Leadership:**
A small India GBS-based team covering data protection, RBC compliance, and junior legal support for contract and RFP reviews.

**Key interfaces:**
Regional and country Legal & Compliance teams; Group Data Protection Office; Group Compliance and Ethics; local management; HR; Finance; Procurement; IS&T and Information Security; operational leadership; external counsel and regulators.

**Employment type:**
Full time

**Purpose of the Role:**

The Legal & Compliance Manager is a qualified lawyer who supports Sodexo's data protection and Responsible Business Conduct (RBC) compliance agenda. The role has primary responsibility for data protection and privacy matters within APMEA, driving the rollout and deployment of RBC compliance policies in the region and local implementation in India, and provision of legal support to India GBS. The role may also support countries in the APMEA region, depending on business priorities and as designated by the Regional General Counsel.

The role has three complementary dimensions: (i) data protection and privacy; (ii) RBC compliance; (iii) legal matters of India GBS; (iv) leadership of a small India GBS-based legal, compliance and data protection team. The role holder will provide practical, risk-growth balanced advice; drive and deploy designated Group programs; implement relevant policies and controls; deliver training; monitor compliance; and report material risks to appropriate stakeholders.

**Key Responsibilities:**

2.1 Data Protection and Privacy

* Advise the business in APMEA (English-speaking markets), on applicable data protection and privacy laws, including Australia’s Privacy Act 1988, India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and, where relevant, the GDPR and other local privacy laws.
* Interpret and implement Sodexo's global data protection policies, standards and Binding Corporate Rules (BCR), identifying where local laws impose additional or different requirements.
* Advise on privacy notices, lawful bases, consent, data subject rights, employee privacy, monitoring, biometrics, CCTV, direct marketing and privacy implications of emerging technologies, including AI.
* Draft, review and negotiate data processing agreements, data sharing arrangements, international data transfer provisions and privacy clauses in client, supplier and technology contracts.
* Support vendor privacy due diligence and third-party privacy risk assessments in collaboration with Procurement, IS&T and Information Security.
* Lead or review Data Protection Impact Assessments and privacy-by-design reviews for new projects, systems and service offerings.
* Manage data subject requests, privacy complaints and personal data breaches, including assessment of regulatory and individual notification obligations.
* Lead data retention implementation for in-scope markets, including defining local retention periods with business owners, recording requirements in OneTrust, facilitating working groups, and monitoring deletion, archiving and remediation actions.
* Support BCR monitoring, quarterly and annual reporting, risk registers, audits, transfer assessments and corrective actions requested by the Group Data Protection Office.
* Cooperate with relevant data protection authorities and coordinate external counsel support where required.

2.2 Responsible Business Conduct (RBC) Compliance

* Drive and deploy Sodexo's Group RBC and compliance programs within the scope designated by the Regional General Counsel, working in coordination with Group Compliance and relevant regional and country stakeholders.
* Serve as the legal and compliance business partner for designated Group compliance programs, including the Third-Party Risk Evaluation Policy, Gifts and Hospitality Policy, Sanctions Policy, and other RBC or ethics-related initiatives assigned by the Regional General Counsel.
* Lead the local implementation, rollout and operationalization of these RBC policies and compliance programs in India, including local procedures, stakeholder guidance, training and awareness, monitoring, remediation and reporting. Ensure that local implementation in India is aligned with Group standards and applicable Indian legal and regulatory requirements.
* Advise management and business teams on compliance risks and controls, including anti-bribery and anti-corruption, conflicts of interest, gifts and hospitality, third-party integrity, competition law, sanctions and other RBC topics within the role’s remit.
* Conduct compliance risk assessments and support integrity due diligence and risk evaluation of relevant third parties, business partners and proposed transactions for the region as directed by regional GC, including HRTP risk assessment/sanction screening, in accordance with group compliance requirements.
* Identify root causes and lessons learned from compliance incidents and support proportionate remediation, control enhancement and disciplinary or contractual follow-up as appropriate.
* Monitor relevant legal and regulatory developments and enforcement trends and assess their potential impact on Sodexo’s operations in India.
* Provide compliance training for the RBC policies for the designated stakeholders.

2.3 Team Leadership and India GBS Legal Support

* Lead, coach and develop a small India GBS-based team whose responsibilities may include data protection, RBC compliance and other legal support activities.
* Provide oversight, guidance and quality assurance to junior legal counsel supporting commercial contract reviews, RFP and bid reviews, and related legal matters handled through India GBS.
* Draft, review and negotiate commercial contracts, supplier contracts and related legal documents for India GBS, and provide practical legal advice on associated contractual risks and issues.
* Plan resources, allocate and prioritize work, manage workloads and establish appropriate service standards to ensure timely and high-quality delivery.
* Build team capability through regular coaching, knowledge sharing, templates, playbooks, training and professional development.
* Foster a collaborative, solution-oriented and business-partnering culture while maintaining strong legal, risk management and compliance standards.
* Coordinate effectively with regional and country Legal & Compliance teams to clarify ownership, escalation routes and service delivery expectations.
* Undertake any other legal, compliance, data protection or related work as may be directed by the APAC Regional General Counsel.

2.4 Training, Awareness and Stakeholder Engagement

* Design and deliver practical training and awareness activities covering data protection, RBC compliance and relevant legal topics.
* Build effective working relationships with local management and key functions, and support a network of privacy, compliance and legal contacts across the in-scope markets.
* Provide timely, commercially aware advice that enables business objectives while protecting Sodexo’s legal, regulatory and reputational interests.
* Escalate material privacy, compliance or legal risks promptly to the Regional General Counsel and relevant Group functions.

3. Qualifications and Experience

3.1 Essential

* Law degree and admission to practise as a lawyer, preferably in India or another common law jurisdiction.
* Approximately 6-8 years’ post-qualification experience gained in-house in a multinational company and/or with a leading law firm.
* Demonstrated hands-on experience in data protection and privacy, including GDPR or comparable privacy frameworks, DPIAs, international data transfers, retention, processor arrangements and breach management.
* Meaningful experience advising on corporate compliance or ethics matters, including deployment and local implementation of compliance policies and controls, risk assessment, training, third-party risk management, sanctions compliance and/or investigations.
* Experience supervising or developing junior legal, compliance or data protection professionals, preferably within a shared services or GBS environment.
* Experience in commercial contract review and RFP or bid support, with the ability to oversee junior legal counsel performing such work.
* Working knowledge of Australian and Indian legal and regulatory requirements relevant to data protection, together with Indian legal and regulatory requirements relevant to corporate compliance, and the ability to support additional APMEA English-speaking markets where assigned.
* Strong drafting, analytical and communication skills, with excellent written and spoken English.

title: Cruelty Response Officer
description:
**Position Objective:**

The Cruelty Response Officer is responsible for investigating complaints of cruelty to animals and violations of animal protection laws, collaborating with authorities, volunteers, animal welfare organisations, and other stakeholders to secure relief for animals and to pursue legal action against offenders. This role primarily involves cruelty case management, complaint drafting, investigations, coordination with local NGOs/activists, and active engagement with authorities to ensure cases of cruelty to animals are taken to their logical end. It also includes working with different law enforcement agencies to coordinate raids and enforcement action against illegal activities.

**Term of Employment:**

Full-time

**Work Schedule:**

Primarily daytime work, with work during evenings, weekends, and public holidays as required.

**Reports To:**

Legal Advisor and Director of Cruelty Response

**Location:**

Mumbai or Delhi (The position involves a combination of office-based, field-based and remote work)

**Primary Responsibilities and Duties:**

* Receive, assess, investigate, and respond to complaints of cruelty to animals involving domestic and wild animals, ranging from neglect and welfare concerns to serious offences, received via phone, e-mail, social media, and other channels.
* Advise members of the public on appropriate legal and practical steps to address cruelty to animals, neglect, and other welfare concerns.
* Analyse photographs, videos, social media content, and other evidence to assess complaints, identify potential violations of animal protection laws, gather information about the accused, and support investigations and case resolution.
* Draft complaints, representations, follow-up communications, and other correspondence to police, forest departments, government authorities, housing societies, educational institutions, and other stakeholders/law enforcement agencies.
* Work with law enforcement authorities, including police, forest department officials, and SPCA representatives, to secure appropriate action in cruelty cases, including the registration of non-cognisable offence reports, first information reports, and preliminary offence reports.
* Coordinate with local animal protection organisations or volunteers to facilitate intervention in cases of cruelty.
* Manage multiple ongoing cases simultaneously, prioritising urgent matters while ensuring timely follow-up.
* Follow up persistently with authorities and other stakeholders to ensure that cruelty cases continue to progress and appropriate action is taken.
* Travel independently across the country, when required, to meet authorities, attend court hearings of cruelty cases, conduct investigations, support rescue efforts, or assist with other case-related activities.
* Travel and coordinate logistics pertaining to sensitisation cum training workshops organised in different parts of the country for law enforcement personnel across different government departments such as police, forest department, animal husbandry, and more.
* Maintain and regularly update the department’s national database of volunteers, animal protection organisations and law enforcement contacts.
* Ensure accurate and comprehensive records of all complaints, correspondence, evidence, actions taken, and case outcomes are maintained.
* Professionally represent PETA India in interactions with members of the public, volunteers, animal welfare organisations, veterinarians, law enforcement agencies, government authorities and other stakeholders.
* Monitor emerging animal welfare issues and identify opportunities for strategic intervention and advocacy.
* Work outside regular office hours, including evenings, weekends, and public holidays, when required to address urgent cases.
* Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree from a recognised institution. A diploma or certificate course in animal protection laws or animal welfare would be an added advantage.
* Minimum one year of relevant professional experience in animal welfare, animal protection, and cruelty response.
* Experience applying animal protection laws while handling cruelty-to-animals or wildlife cases, either professionally or through sustained volunteer work.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and the ability to conduct online research and investigations.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Hindi; proficiency in additional Indian languages preferred.
* Excellent drafting, research, analytical, organisational, and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.
* Ability to deal patiently, communicate professionally and effectively with animal protection organisations, volunteers, complainants, veterinarians, law enforcement agencies, government authorities, and other stakeholders.
* Strong problem-solving skills, resourcefulness, and persistence in handling complex matters and driving them towards resolution.
* Passion for facilitating law enforcement work, preventing cruelty to animals, and helping animals in need
* Compassionate, responsible, self-driven and detail-oriented
* Outgoing and personable manner with strong interpersonal skills
* Adherence to a vegan lifestyle
* Ability and willingness to travel independently across the country, as needed, to handle cruelty cases
* Supportive position
  *vis-à-vis*
  PETA India’s philosophy and the ability to advocate for it’s positions in a professional manner
* Commitment to the objectives of the organisation

**About the Role**

The Deputy MLRO / AML Compliance Manager supports the MLRO in maintaining an effective, risk-based AML/ATF and sanctions compliance framework for Opus. The role provides day-to-day 2nd line oversight of client and investor due diligence, enhanced due diligence, ongoing monitoring, sanctions screening, suspicious activity escalation, training, record-keeping, and management information, while preserving independence from 1st line operational decision-making.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Support the MLRO in implementing and maintaining AML/ATF policies, procedures, systems and controls consistent with Bermuda regulatory expectations and the administrator’s financial crime risk profile.
* Provide independent 2nd line review and challenge over client, fund and investor onboarding, including CDD, EDD, beneficial ownership, source of funds, source of wealth, PEP, jurisdictional and intermediary risk considerations.
* Manage and triage AML/ATF and sanctions escalations from the 1st line, ensuring matters are assessed, documented, escalated and resolved in a timely manner.
* Assist the MLRO with suspicious activity assessment and internal reporting processes, including preparation of case analysis and documentation to support any decision to report to the appropriate authority.
* Oversee ongoing monitoring and periodic review activity, including risk-rating changes, trigger events, overdue reviews, exceptions, remediation actions and higher-risk relationships.
* Support sanctions screening governance, including escalation standards, potential match review, disposition quality, list management oversight and reporting or freezing escalation where applicable.
* Prepare AML/ATF management information for the MLRO, senior management and board or committee reporting, including key risks, issues, breaches, SAR-related metrics, sanctions matters, training completion, testing results and remediation status.

* Maintain appropriate records of AML/ATF approvals, escalations, risk assessments, monitoring outcomes, training, testing, breaches and remediation in line with record-keeping requirements.
* Deputise for the MLRO when required, including acting as an escalation point and supporting regulatory engagement, while ensuring significant matters remain subject to appropriate MLRO and governance oversight.

The role should be held by an appropriately senior and experienced AML/ATF professional with sufficient authority, access to information, independence and resources to provide effective challenge. **Position Overview**
The Senior IT Compliance Specialist is a hands-on, globally oriented role responsible for translating regulatory, customer, and internal security requirements into sustainable controls, defensible evidence, and audit-ready operations. The position partners across security, legal, business, support, engineering, infrastructure, and cloud teams to advance compliance outcomes without creating unnecessary operational friction.
  
  
This role is designed for an experienced practitioner who can independently lead workstreams, influence control owners, communicate with auditors and customers, and improve the way compliance work is scoped, documented, monitored, and automated.
  
  
**Role mandate**
Make compliance executable: clarify scope and ownership, design practical controls, maintain evidence, anticipate change, and keep priority programs ready for assessment throughout the year.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Compliance leadership and program delivery**

* Lead and manage IT compliance initiatives to ensure adherence to internal policies, standards, contractual obligations, and applicable international or government security frameworks.
* Own assigned workstreams from requirement intake and scoping through control mapping, gap assessment, remediation, evidence readiness, and ongoing governance.
* Maintain compliance strategies, roadmaps, and operating plans that align security requirements with business priorities, technology architecture, and delivery commitments.
* Establish clear accountability with business owners, IT asset owners, and control owners; track decisions, risks, dependencies, and remediation commitments to closure.

**Assessments, certifications, and audit readiness**

* Drive certification and assurance efforts by coordinating internal audits, external assessments, customer reviews, risk assessments, and security documentation submissions.
* Plan and facilitate readiness activities for ISO 27001, NIST SP 800-171, CMMC, TISAX, NIS2, and other requirements assigned to the team.
* Coordinate requests with assessors and third-party auditors, validate the completeness and quality of evidence, and ensure responses are accurate, consistent, and traceable.
* Manage findings and corrective actions using a risk-based approach, including root-cause analysis, remediation planning, validation, exception handling, and status reporting.
* Promote continuous readiness by defining evidence expectations, review cadences, health indicators, and escalation paths rather than relying on point-in-time audit preparation.

**Control design, implementation, and monitoring**

* Interpret framework and regulatory requirements and translate them into clear, testable control objectives, control activities, evidence requirements, and ownership models.
* Partner with engineering, infrastructure, application, cloud, security operations, identity, data, and support teams to embed controls into technology processes and system lifecycles.
* Assess control design and operating effectiveness, identify gaps or duplicated effort, and recommend practical remediation that balances risk, compliance, and operational needs.
* Support continuous monitoring through defined metrics, automated evidence collection, exception reporting, and periodic control reviews.
* Contribute to reusable control mappings and a unified control approach to reduce duplication across overlapping frameworks and customer obligations.

**Documentation and stakeholder support**

* Maintain and enhance System Security Plans (SSPs), Information Security Management System, policies, standards, procedures, control narratives, risk assessments, plans of action, evidence repositories, and governance records.
* Serve as a subject matter expert on IT compliance, advising internal teams on scope, control expectations, audit evidence, risk treatment, and compliance-by-design.
* Support customers, contracting stakeholders, and Authorizing Officials (AOs) by providing approved compliance documentation and clear guidance for security evaluations.
* Prepare concise status reports, risk statements, decision materials, and executive updates that distinguish confirmed facts, open issues, ownership, and required action.
* Develop practical guidance and targeted training for control owners and technical teams to improve execution quality and audit readiness.

**Regulatory intelligence and process improvement**

* Coordinate with Legal, Privacy, Procurement, Internal Audit, Security, and business stakeholders to validate interpretations and convert changes into actionable implementation plans.
* Identify opportunities to automate recurring compliance activities, streamline evidence collection, improve workflow quality, and reduce manual or duplicative work.
* Use lessons learned, audit results, metrics, and stakeholder feedback to improve control design, documentation quality, governance, and team operating practices.
* Perform other responsibilities or special assignments as requested by leadership.

**Required Qualifications**

* 5–10 years of relevant experience in IT compliance, IT audit, cybersecurity governance, technology risk, or a closely related discipline.
* Demonstrated experience leading compliance assessments, audits, certifications, or regulatory readiness efforts in a complex, multinational technology environment.
* Working knowledge of several of the following: ISO 27001/27002, NIST SP 800-171, CMMC, TISAX, NIS2, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, SOC reporting, IT general controls, or comparable security frameworks.
* Experience translating requirements into control designs, test procedures, evidence expectations, risk statements, and remediation plans.
* Experience creating or maintaining compliance documentation such as SSPs, policies, standards, procedures, control narratives, risk assessments, and audit evidence packages.
* Ability to manage multiple workstreams, organize complex information, meet deadlines, and escalate material risks or dependencies with sound judgment.
* Strong written and verbal English communication skills, including the ability to work effectively across cultures, functions, technical disciplines, and time zones.
* Bachelor’s degree in information systems, cybersecurity, computer science, accounting, risk management, business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Relevant certification such as CISA, CRISC, CISSP, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor, CISM, or a comparable credential.
* Experience supporting cloud or hybrid environments, regulated data, government contracting obligations, automotive assurance, or European cybersecurity requirements.
* Experience with governance, risk, and compliance platforms; workflow automation; data visualization; scripting; or automated evidence collection.
* Familiarity with third-party risk, privacy, Responsible AI governance, mergers and acquisitions, or customer security assurance.
* Experience supporting distributed teams through clear documentation, structured handoffs, measurable service expectations, and overlapping working hours when required.

**Indicators of Success**

* Assigned compliance obligations are clearly scoped, mapped to accountable owners, and supported by current documentation.
* Assessments and audits are executed with timely, accurate, and traceable evidence and minimal avoidable rework.
* Control gaps, risks, exceptions, and remediation actions are transparent, risk-prioritized, and progressed to closure.
* Compliance requirements are embedded earlier in technology, sourcing, and change decisions.
* Recurring work becomes more standardized, measurable, automated, and sustainable across the global delivery model.

**Work Style and Collaboration Expectations**
The successful candidate is proactive, structured, pragmatic, and comfortable operating with a high degree of independence. Because the role supports global stakeholders, the individual must be able to manage priorities across time zones, document decisions and handoffs clearly, protect confidential information, and maintain dependable communication during agreed collaboration windows. Market Data Contract/Vendor Manager
  
  
Chennai, India
  
  
You will join Glencore’s global Market Data team supporting the Oil division. The role is responsible for vendor management, contract negotiation and administration, and oversight of the market data portfolio to ensure value, compliance, and cost efficiency.
  
  
Working with trading, risk, legal, and technology teams, you will support vendor selection, licence management, contract renewals, spend analysis, and optimisation initiatives. Success in the role requires strong commercial acumen, attention to detail, stakeholder management skills, and the ability to deliver results in a fast-paced global environment.
  
  
**Responsibilities:**

* Working closely with the London-based Market Data Procurement team, managing relationships with market data, exchange, benchmark, and analytics vendors across Trading, Risk, Finance, Operations, and Technology teams.
* Supporting vendor selection, contract renewals, commercial negotiations, and sourcing initiatives to ensure cost-effective service delivery and optimal commercial outcomes.
* Conducting licence reviews, usage assessments, benchmarking, spend analysis, and cost optimisation initiatives across the market data portfolio.
* Managing market data agreements, exchange licences, vendor contracts, Statements of Work, and related contractual documentation.
* Working closely with Legal, Compliance, Procurement, and Information Security teams to ensure contractual, regulatory, and commercial requirements are appropriately maintained.
* Coordinating vendor onboarding, due diligence, and third-party risk assessment activities.
* Supporting market data audits, licence compliance reviews, entitlement management, and the tracking of contractual obligations.
* Gathering and validating business requirements and ensuring licensing solutions align with business needs.
* Maintaining accurate contract, licence, vendor inventory, and governance records.
* Driving process automation, governance enhancements, and operational efficiencies across the market data function.
* Building strong relationships with vendors, business users, and senior management to support effective service delivery and decision-making.
* Ensuring compliance with internal policies, contractual obligations, exchange requirements, and regulatory standards.
* Supporting the development of market data governance frameworks, controls, processes, and reporting capabilities.
* Undertaking other ad hoc duties as required.

**Key relationships:**

* Market data team – London, Chennai, AMER
* Business stakeholders all locations
* Legal
* Metals

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree or relevant work experience

**Work experience:**

* 3 to 10 years of experience in Market Data, including vendor management, market data administration, entitlement management, inventory analysis, or commercial management
* Experience of inventory management tools (TRG Optimize, Calero)
* Strong reporting, data analysis, spend optimisation, and process improvement experience
* Experience with market data platforms, vendor contracts, usage analytics, and automation tools is highly desirable
* Familiarity with financial market data providers (e.g., Bloomberg, LSEG, FactSet, S&P Global, ICE, Morningstar) and data governance processes is an advantage

**Competencies:**

* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
* Excellent organisational and time management abilities
* High attention to detail with a focus on data accuracy
* Strong analytical and problem-solving capability
* Commercial mindset focused on cost optimisation and business value
* Good financial acumen and data interpretation skills
* Advanced Excel and strong technology literacy
* Interest in financial markets and market data trends
* Proactive, adaptable, and eager to learn
* Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment
* Experience with data governance, compliance, and vendor management is advantageous

**Who We Are**
Glencore is one of the world’s largest global diversified natural resource companies and a major producer and marketer of more than 60 commodities. Through a network of assets, customers and suppliers that spans the globe, we produce, process, recycle, source, market and distribute the commodities that advance everyday life.
  
  
With over 140,000 employees and contractors and a strong footprint in over 30 countries in both established and emerging regions for natural resources, our marketing and industrial activities are supported by a global network of offices.
  
  
Glencore’s customers are principally industrial consumers, such as those in the automotive, steel, power generation, battery manufacturing and oil sectors. We also provide financing, logistics and other services to producers and consumers of commodities.

title: Senior Manager - Legal
description:
**About Cognizant Corporate**
Cognizant Corporate is a global community united by a shared purpose: to make a meaningful impact. We are committed to excellence and driven by outcomes that matter. Collaboration is at the heart of how we work, and our forward-thinking mindset fuels continuous learning, innovation, and growth.
  
  
At Cognizant, careers transcend titles. We empower our people to think strategically, inspire others, and lead with purpose – always guided by our core values. Join us in shaping future of business.
  
  
**About The Role**
As a Senior Manager - Legal, you will drive impactful contributions and focus on outcomes. You will be a key member of the Technology Transactions team, collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders including business, finance, procurement etc. The candidate will oversee the negotiation, review, and management of vendor and partner agreements, together with client contracts related to third party provisioning for Cognizant's business operations. The candidate will serve as a trusted legal advisor to the business, ensuring the protection of Cognizant's interests through the assessment of legal and commercial risks and the implementation of appropriate contractual safeguards and mitigation measures.
  
  
As a team of self-starters, you can work with impact with our vibrant people and culture all while enjoying unmatched learning opportunities.
  
  
**In This Role, You Will**

* Support strategic transactions and business opportunities by proactively engaging with deal teams, evaluating contractual and commercial risks, and providing timely visibility of material issues and potential exposures to senior management.
* Partner with Cognizant's business, procurement, alliances, and delivery teams to develop and implement contractual frameworks that support business objectives and enable sustainable growth.
* Draft, review, negotiate, and advise on a broad range of global commercial agreements, including software license and subscription agreements, alliance and teaming agreements, subcontracting arrangements, vendor services agreements, RFPs, statements of work, and non-disclosure agreements.
* Identify, assess, and advise on legal, commercial, operational, regulatory, and compliance risks arising from contractual arrangements, and develop pragmatic mitigation strategies that balance risk and business objectives.
* Collaborate closely with cross-functional stakeholders, including procurement, finance, tax, information security, privacy, compliance, and business leadership teams, to obtain subject matter input and appropriately incorporate such requirements into contractual documentation.
* Foster knowledge sharing and collaboration within the legal function to drive consistency, operational efficiency, and continuous enhancement of legal service delivery.
* Champion AI Fluency and continuous improvement initiatives, including process optimization, standardization, automation, and the adoption of best practices to enhance the effectiveness of the legal organization.
* Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of legal professionals, ensuring the delivery of high-quality legal support, effective management of escalations, and meaningful career development for direct reports.
* Develop and deliver training, coaching, and mentorship programs to enhance contracting capability, legal awareness, and risk management acumen across the legal team and broader business organization.
* Embrace our vibrant culture by striving for excellence, focusing on meaningful outcomes, and collaborating effectively. Take ownership, build relationships, and focus on personal growth to drive business strategy and foster an inclusive culture, creating unmatched career opportunities and impactful work.

**What You Must Have To Be Considered**

* Having extensive contracting knowledge and experience especially handling technology contracts
* Having a strong legal and business (understanding of transactional nuances) acumen to assess risks and recommend possible mitigations.
* Articulation of the highest order both written and verbal
* Ability to work in a dynamic and fast-paced environment
* Demonstrating leadership and having strong organizational skills.
* Demonstrating complete ownership and accountability by being the single point of contact for resolution of issues.
* Exceptional interpersonal skills to effectively communicate and coordinate complex issues with diverse levels of management and to collaborate and guide the junior attorneys
* A strong sense of ownership, desire to create meaningful outcomes, and passion for work that serves a greater good for customers, communities, or global challenges.
* The embodiment of Cognizant’s Values of: Work as One, Dare to Innovate, Raise the Bar, Do The right Thing, & Own It

**These will help you succeed**

We believe hybrid work is the way forward as we strive to provide flexibility wherever possible. Based on this role’s business requirements, this is a hybrid position requiring at least 3 days a week in Cognizant office in Bengaluru, Karnataka (or any other city in India). Regardless of your working arrangement, we are here to support a healthy work-life balance though our various wellbeing programs.
  
  
The working arrangements for this role are accurate as of the date of posting. This may change based on the project you’re engaged in, as well as business and client requirements. Rest assured; we will always be clear about role expectations.
